content.user_title: Plan a Manifest V3 Website Trust Checker
content.value_statement: Planning a website safety extension requires coordinating browser components, page signals, and external services. This guide outlines a no-build approach without supplying extension source code.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a no-build extension approach using vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
Describes trust scoring from SSL status, RDAP domain age, and page transparency signals.
Identifies service workers, content scripts, and popup UI as cooperating extension components.
Describes on-page warnings for high-risk domains.
Outlines settings for user-supplied Google Safe Browsing and PhishTank API keys.
Describes local persistence for settings and extension state without a backend.
limitations: The supplied package contains only a guide; scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
Production readiness, scoring accuracy, and Chrome Web Store compliance cannot be verified from this documentation.
Threat intelligence integrations require user-supplied API keys and external service access.
React, Vue, and TypeScript build pipelines require manual migration from the described vanilla approach.

use_cases.title: Scope a browser safety prototype
use_cases.description: Translate the described scoring signals and extension components into an implementation checklist before development.

use_cases.title: Review safety product requirements
use_cases.description: Assess domain age, page transparency, warning behavior, and threat API requirements without assuming validated detection accuracy.

use_cases.title: Study Manifest V3 architecture
use_cases.description: Use the guide to discuss service workers, content scripts, popup interfaces, and local settings.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the proposed website trust checker. Separate documented features from files actually included in this package.

prompt_templates.title: Create a component plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a vanilla Manifest V3 prototype from this guide. Assign responsibilities to the service worker, content script, popup, and settings interface.

prompt_templates.title: Review scoring assumptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review SSL status, RDAP domain age, and transparency signals as trust inputs. Identify false positives, unavailable data, and unverified assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a validation strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose tests for a future implementation covering permissions, API key handling, network failures, local storage, and warning behavior. Do not claim tests already passed.

output_examples.input: What does this package actually include?
output_examples.output: The package contains a public guide describing a Manifest V3 website trust checker. Extension source, scripts, and templates are not included.

output: Background service worker: coordinate RDAP lookups and external threat checks.
Content script: collect transparency signals and display warnings.
Popup interface: present the proposed trust score.
Settings interface: manage user-supplied API keys and local preferences.

output_examples.input: Can these trust signals prove that a website is safe?
output_examples.output: No. Domain age, SSL status, and transparency signals are heuristics. A future implementation needs validation and must communicate uncertainty.

best_practices: Confirm which implementation files are available before scheduling development or release.
Validate scoring assumptions against representative legitimate and malicious websites.
Review extension permissions, API key handling, and external request privacy before deployment.
anti_patterns: Treating the guide as an included, tested extension codebase.
Presenting a high trust score as proof that a website is safe.
Publishing generated extension code without testing permissions, API failures, and warning behavior.

faq.question: Does this package include a working extension?
faq.answer: No. The supplied folder contains only the public guide, despite broader source code claims elsewhere in the document.

faq.question: What technology does the guide describe?
faq.answer: It describes Manifest V3 with vanilla JavaScript, HTML, CSS, service workers, content scripts, and a popup interface.

faq.question: Which signals contribute to the proposed trust score?
faq.answer: The guide lists SSL status, domain age through RDAP, and transparency signals such as privacy policies and return information.

faq.question: Are API keys required?
faq.answer: The guide specifies user-supplied Google Safe Browsing and PhishTank API keys for enhanced threat detection.

faq.question: Does the proposed architecture require a build pipeline?
faq.answer: No build step is described for the vanilla approach. React, Vue, and TypeScript workflows require manual migration.

faq.question: Is Chrome Web Store readiness verified?
faq.answer: No. The supplied documentation does not include implementation files or test results that establish store compliance or production readiness.
